question: Same aircraft, same day: if flight 3851 PHX-SFO on 2026-01-03 were only 20 minutes late instead of 142, how far down N8633A's day would that propagate?

input.reason: counterfactual: 3851 only 20 min late instead of 142

content.text:
**It would stop one leg later, and cost 5 downstream minutes instead of 565.**

N8633A's 2026-01-03 rotation is seven legs: MSY-PHX (WN3851, 05:40, arrived 11 early), then PHX-SFO (WN3851, 08:55), SFO-PHX (WN4106, 10:55), PHX-LGB (WN172, 14:40), LGB-LAS (WN65, 15:45), LAS-DAL (WN65, 17:35), DAL-HOU (WN65, 22:55).

Simulated from schedule with only a 20-minute departure delay on `2026-01-03|WN|3851|PHX|SFO|0855`, the cascade reaches exactly one leg: `2026-01-03|WN|4106|SFO|PHX|1055` departs 5 minutes late, and the SFO turn plus the PHX ground time absorb the rest. WN172, both WN65 legs out of LGB and LAS, and the DAL-HOU finisher all go back to on time. Total downstream exposure: 5 minutes over 1 leg.

For contrast, the same simulation run at the actual 142 minutes propagates through all five remaining legs — 127, 117, 112, 107 and 102 minutes, 565 downstream minutes total — which lines up with what the day actually recorded: WN4106 out 144 late (133 of it coded late_aircraft), WN172 135 (128 late_aircraft), WN65 LGB-LAS 140 (124), WN65 LAS-DAL 144 (116), WN65 DAL-HOU 155 (114). So roughly 560 of the 565 downstream minutes are attributable to the delay above 20 minutes on the PHX-SFO leg; the small residual gaps between the projection and the actuals are the carrier-coded minutes added at each station (1, 0, 9, 10, 25).

One caveat on the sim: it projects from the scheduled baseline with turn times estimated from observed ground times, so it is showing you a clean-schedule counterfactual, not a replay with the day's other real-world frictions (the PHX-SFO delay itself was coded 141 minutes NAS, and NAS conditions at SFO that morning would not disappear just because this tail left on time).
